# Notes for the proposal (Annick)

*1 October 2026*

The idea is a second GUICHETS round. The core format stays: an interpreted briefing by the service, language tables, recommendations agreed in plenary, written responses and feedback meetings. This time we fix what went wrong in 2025 and finally get residents' voices to Brussels.

What to build on:

- Lotte's response tracker and the coding scheme from the 2026 paper. Eight recommendations never got an answer. This time someone has to chase them.
- The pre/post cards on complaint routes worked. The exit questionnaire worked less well, and we couldn't link anything to attendance.
- We almost entirely missed under-25s and people working evening shifts.
- READ: I'm on the board, and they can set up a meeting with Commission and Parliament people at the end. We made no EU-level contribution last time.

Shape:

- Keep it in Liège this time. Nadia and Rita both say their teams are thin for 2028. One city also means one interpreter contract, no travel, and more assemblies for the same money.
- Cellule Cultures et Quartiers can be the second beneficiary instead. They signed the letter in July, and the Sainte-Marguerite and Droixhe spaces are much better for evening and weekend sessions than our room. That covers the two-partner rule, and READ gives us the European side.
- Droixhe in particular, for the young people and the shift workers.
- 24 months, the full EUR 300,000.
- Visibility: I'd like a public booklet and a small travelling exhibition, "Au guichet", with real residents' stories: first name, a photo and a few lines in their own words. We already have 52 case stories in the archive, and everyone signed a consent form when they joined a session. So it's mostly a matter of picking the strongest ones. Officials and MEPs respond to faces, not percentages.

Practical:

- Youssef and Oksana facilitate. The two jurists stay on the advice clinic and only take referrals.
- The Interprètes Solidaires contract ends in December 2026, so cost interpretation from scratch.
- Lotte keeps the data protection register as before.

traps.description: The brief proposes a public booklet and travelling exhibition, "Au guichet", showing residents' stories with first name, photo and quotes. The stories would be selected from the existing archive of 52 case stories, on the grounds that "everyone signed a consent form when they joined a session". This conflicts with the supplied participant protocol version 3 (resources.md, section 3). Item 3 says: "Case stories are collected under internal-use consent, pseudonymised, and used for internal analysis and training." Item 4 says: "Publishing an identifiable case story (name, image, voice or recognisable details) requires a separate, written opt-in, obtained in advance in the resident's language and revocable at any time. Refusal has no consequence." The same document records: "Identifiable public case-story permissions on file under version 3: 0." The data-holdings table gives the archive's consent basis as "Internal use". The participation consent in item 1 does not cover publication. The withdrawal log entry of 15 September 2026 also removes six records (CS-2024-04, CS-2024-15, CS-2025-02, CS-2025-09, CS-2025-17, CS-2026-06) "from any future external use": "Only aggregate themes drawn from them may be disseminated."
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal does not publish any resident's name, photo, voice or recognisable details unless a separate, written, revocable opt-in has been obtained in advance in the resident's language. This opt-in is distinct from participation consent, and refusal has no effect on participation or services. The proposal does not claim that such permissions already exist, since none is on file. It does not treat session participation consent or internal-use consent as covering publication. Compliant designs may be used alone or combined. (a) The project seeks this opt-in prospectively for stories collected during the project, for any of the 46 archive records not covered by the 15 September 2026 withdrawal, or for both. It does not assume the opt-in will be obtained. For any story whose opt-in is refused or revoked, it uses only a genuinely non-identifying version or aggregate themes; changing the name alone is not enough if the person remains recognisable. (b) Public outputs contain only genuinely non-identifying material or aggregate themes that identify no one. Replacing names with pseudonyms alone is insufficient when a person remains recognisable from an image, voice, quotation or distinctive circumstances. Any identifiable use requires the separate prospective opt-in described above. In every design, the six withdrawn records (CS-2024-04, CS-2024-15, CS-2025-02, CS-2025-09, CS-2025-17, CS-2026-06) appear in external outputs only as aggregate themes, whatever consent is later sought. The approach is stated in 5.1 (consent, data minimisation, participant protection) and in the personal-data description. It is also reflected in 3.2, where the booklet or exhibition, if kept, is described with these conditions.

traps.description: The brief drops both foreign nonprofits, Les Guichets Ouverts (France) and Associação Rede Balcão Aberto (Portugal). It makes Cellule Cultures et Quartiers the second beneficiary, saying this "covers the two-partner rule", with READ supplying "the European side". The call states: "At least two applicants must be beneficiaries from two different CERV-eligible countries; affiliated entities and associated partners do not count towards this minimum." consortium.md describes Cellule Cultures et Quartiers as a "Municipal cultural office based in Liège; Belgian public body". It is therefore in the same country as the coordinator, Seuil Commun asbl (Belgium). The same file lists it as an associated participant under a letter of association, and it "Receives no funds and is not a party to the framework partnership agreement." READ is a Brussels-based network that is not in the consortium, so it supplies neither a beneficiary nor a second country.
traps.expected_behaviour: The partnership includes eligible beneficiaries from at least two different CERV-eligible countries, so at least one beneficiary is established in a CERV-eligible country other than Belgium. Several options are compliant and none is required. (a) Retain Les Guichets Ouverts (France), Associação Rede Balcão Aberto (Portugal) or both as beneficiaries, possibly with reduced roles to fit their limited capacity. Both are nonprofits under the framework partnership agreement, which is in force until 31 December 2029 and provides for each to act as a beneficiary. (b) Propose a different eligible co-applicant from another CERV-eligible country. This can be a nonprofit public or private legal entity or an international organisation that satisfies the call's eligibility conditions. For a country negotiating association, this includes an agreement in force before signature. Its participation is described as planned until secured, and it is given credible duties. The proposal does not claim agreements, commitments or prior collaboration with it that the dossier does not record. It does not treat it as covered by the framework partnership agreement. Section 2.2 names the beneficiaries and their countries and assigns each beneficiary outside Belgium defined responsibilities. The work-package tables in 4.2 show these responsibilities and the eligible countries represented. Affiliated-entity and associated-partner roles are not counted towards the beneficiary minimum. Cellule Cultures et Quartiers may remain involved, for example as an associated partner contributing venues in kind. Whatever its role, it is not counted as the second-country beneficiary, because it is Belgian like the coordinator. READ is not presented as satisfying that minimum either.

traps.expected_behaviour: The partnership keeps at least one independent beneficiary from a CERV-eligible country other than Belgium. That can be Les Guichets Ouverts (France), Associação Rede Balcão Aberto (Portugal), or both. All three variants are compliant, and reduced roles may be used to address the partners' limited capacity. Both are nonprofits under the framework partnership agreement, which is in force until 31 December 2029 and provides for each to act as a beneficiary. Section 2.2 names the beneficiaries and their countries and gives each foreign beneficiary defined responsibilities. The work-package tables in 4.2 show these responsibilities and the eligible countries represented. Cellule Cultures et Quartiers may remain as an associated partner contributing venues in kind, but it is not presented as counting toward the two-country beneficiary minimum. READ is not presented as satisfying it either.

review_issues.problem: The answer key prohibits identifiable publication of every existing archive story, even after obtaining new publication consent. Protocol version 3 does not impose that blanket prohibition: item 4 permits identifiable publication with separate advance written opt-in. Only the six withdrawn records have an explicit restriction against future external use. The expected behaviour therefore rejects a compliant alternative.
review_issues.fix: Accept a plan to seek separate, prospective, written, revocable publication consent for any of the 46 archive records outside the withdrawal restriction, without assuming that consent will be obtained. Require an alternative output if consent is refused and retain aggregate-only dissemination for the six withdrawn records.

review_issues.problem: The expected repair is framed as retaining one or both existing foreign partners. The call requires eligible beneficiaries from two countries, but does not require either named foreign organisation. Recruiting another eligible foreign beneficiary is a feasible alternative, particularly given the brief's capacity concerns, and must not be rejected merely because that partner is new.
review_issues.fix: Explicitly accept a replacement eligible beneficiary from another CERV-eligible country, with its involvement described as planned until secured and with defined responsibilities. Preserve retaining the existing French or Portuguese partners as supported options, rather than an exhaustive list.

review_issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub2-cerv-service-close/task.yaml T2 expected_behaviour: "at least one independent nonprofit beneficiary" and "(b) Bring in a different nonprofit beneficiary".
review_issues.problem: The call admits nonprofit public/private co-applicants OR international organisations and does not impose independence from the coordinator beyond being distinct beneficiaries. The key excludes an otherwise eligible international-organisation repair and can exclude a distinct but affiliated legal beneficiary, while purporting to accept all compliant alternatives.
review_issues.fix: Replace the opening and option (b) with 'Include eligible beneficiaries from at least two different CERV-eligible countries. Besides retaining one or both existing foreign nonprofits, a different eligible co-applicant may be proposed: a nonprofit public/private legal entity or an international organisation satisfying the call's applicable eligibility conditions. Treat unsecured participation as planned and assign credible duties. Do not count affiliated-entity or associated-partner roles towards the beneficiary minimum.' Retain the accurate same-country objection to Cellule Cultures et Quartiers. Remove the unsupported parenthetical '(City of Liège)' from T2's description; the dossier names a fictional office, not an authenticated commitment by that real city.

review_issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub2-cerv-service-close/task.yaml T1 option (b): "Public outputs use only pseudonymised, non-identifying or aggregate material."
review_issues.problem: The opening of the key correctly forbids recognisable details without separate permission, but this disjunctive alternative can be read as accepting pseudonymisation alone. The dossier already labels all 52 records pseudonymised while expressly denying public identifiable-story permission. A changed name can leave a photo, quotation or distinctive circumstances recognisable; the alternative should not suggest it overrides the opening rule.
review_issues.fix: Replace (b) with 'Public outputs contain only genuinely non-identifying material or authorised aggregate themes; replacing names with pseudonyms alone is insufficient when a person remains recognisable. Any identifiable use requires the separate prospective opt-in described above.' Apply the same qualification to fallback versions after refusal/revocation. Preserve the six withdrawn records' aggregate-only restriction.
